MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  AUGUST 8, 2017

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by MAYOR ZERUNYAN at 5:40 p.m. and the City Council convened into Closed
Session in the City Manager’s Office, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills
Estates.

City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard

14.  CLOSED SESSION (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER)

A.  DISCUSSION WITH RESPECT TO PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT: ANNUAL CITY
  MANAGER EVALUATION (Pursuant to Government Code Section 54937)

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ AND CITY MANAGER PRICHARD WERE
  AUTHORIZED TO FINALIZE GOALS FOR FY17-18.

B.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - PENDING LITIGATION (Pursuant to
  Government Code Section 54956.9(a)) Merriweather Properties v. City of Rolling
  Hills Estates, Cal Water

  DEFERRED TO FUTURE MEETING.

  ***

  At 7:00 p.m., the COUNCIL reconvened into open session in the City Council
  Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, CA with MAYOR
  ZERUNYAN, MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL, COUNCIL
  MEMBER SCHMITZ AND COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN present.

  ***

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Senior Planner Jeannie Naughton
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
AUGUST 8, 2017
 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

A Boy Scout from Troop #128 led the audience in the Pledge of Allegiance.

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  MAYOR ZERUNYAN presented a proclamation congratulating USC on the
  opening of “USC Village”.

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JULY 25, 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ.

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JUNE 27, 2017 AS
  PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – JULY AND AUGUST

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ inquired as to the cost of the City’s membership
  in South Bay Cities Council of Governments (SBCCOG) as compared to the cost
  for other association memberships noting that the cost of the SBCCOG
  membership is considerably higher than the other associations. Following
  discussion concerning the funding formula and the value of the SBCCOG
  membership, staff was directed to schedule the SBCCOG Executive Director to
  attend a future City Council meeting to explain the funding formula and provide
  information on the value of membership

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ.

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 58759 THROUGH 58759 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $145,924.22; SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 070117 THROUGH 070717;
  57143 (VOID), 58616 THROUGH 58672, 58695 (VOID); 58719 (VOID);
  58720 THROUGH 58753 IN THE AMOUNT OF $518,934.65 FOR A
  GRAND TOTAL OF $664,858.87 WITH PROPER AUDIT; AND WITH THE
  EXCEPTION OF WARRANT 58625 TO SOUTH BAY CITIES COUNCIL OF
  GOVERNMENTS IN THE AMOUNT OF $8,057.00 WHICH WAS ASKED
  TO BE BROUGHT BACK WITH FURTHER INFORMATION REGARDING
  THE SBCCOG EXPENDITURES.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
AUGUST 8, 2017
 6.  CONSENT CALENDAR: The following routine matters will be acted upon by one
  vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council. There will be no
  separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior
  to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ.

  TO APPROVE ITEMS A-D.

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to
  the City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be
  read by title only.

  APPROVED

B.  2017-18 MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING

  APPROVED

C.  SALARY RESOLUTIONS FY 2017-18

  ADOPTED RESOLUTION NO. 2403 – COMPENSATION FOR
  PROFESSIONAL CLASSIFICATIONS; RESOLUTION NO. 2404 –
  COMPENSATION FOR MANAGEMENT CLASSIFICATIONS; RESOLUTION
  NO. 2405 – COMPENSATION FOR CLASSIFIED GROUP; AND
  RESOLUTION NO. 2406 – COMPENSATION FOR PART-TIME GROUP.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read Resolution No. 2403, 2404, 2405 and 2406 by title
  only.

D.  AUTHORITY TO MICRO-IMAGE AND DESTROY ORIGINAL RECORDS

  GRANTED AUTHORITY TO MICRO-IMAGE AND DESTROY THE
  ORIGINAL RECORDS FOR “ZONE CLEARANCE FOR MINOR WORK”
  FROM 2013 THROUGH MAY, 2015.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

7.  AUDIENCE ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

  NONE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
AUGUST 8, 2017
 8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

  NONE

9.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PURCHASE OF A TRACTOR LOADER

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize staff to purchase from John
  Deere a new 210L Tractor Loader with accessories at a cost not to exceed
  $102,00 and after-purchase items for the tractor to not exceed $8,000 for a
  grand total of approximately $110,000.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Administrative Services
  Director Whitehead noted that the standard warranty is typically one-year, but
  staff is looking into an extended warranty given the intended off-road use of the
  tractor.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ.

  TO AUTHORIZE STAFF TO PURCHASE FROM JOHN DEERE A NEW
  210L TRACTOR LOADER WITH ACCESSORIES AT A COST NOT TO
  EXCEED $102,000 AND AFTER-PURCHASE ITEMS FOR THE TRACTOR
  TO NOT EXCEED $8,000 FOR A GRAND TOTAL OF APPROXIMATELY
  $110,000.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

10.  OLD BUSINESS

  NONE

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

A.  CC&R REVIEW - PA-05-16 (MERRILL GARDENS/THE VILLAGE)

  Senior Planner Naughton presented the City Attorney’s memo (as per agenda
  material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Mr. Rose explained that both
  the Condominium Association and the unit owners will be bound by the
  conditions of approval which include a requirement that city codes be adhered
  to.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
AUGUST 8, 2017
   City Manager Prichard noted that regardless of the structure of the CC&R’s, the
  City still has police powers to enforce its codes.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, Mr. Rose explained that Exhibit
  B provides the framework for the number of votes each owner gets proportional
  to the square footage of the lots and allows for the lots to be subdivided allowing
  a proportional share of the votes for each owner.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL, Mr. Rose confirmed that
  Continental Development has agreed to the changes proposed by the City
  Attorney as shown in the staff report; and those changes have been
  incorporated into the CC&R’s. He further noted that the terms of the agreement
  that was reached concerning the library parking issue have been incorporated
  into the CC&R’s.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE REPORT

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS: This item provides the
  opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to
  other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of
  currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide
  governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and
  their various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or
  have an interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

A.  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ reported that she and COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN attended a Palos Verdes Transit Authority meeting at which it
  was reported that Supervisor Janice Hahn has again provided funding for this
  year. She further reported that public transportation ridership is down
  countywide.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN suggested that Councilmembers encourage
  Supervisor Hahn to continue this funding.

B.  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF reported on the July meeting of the South Bay Cities
  Council of Governments (SBCCOG). Items discussed included a coalition to
  address storm water related issues, and the impact the SBCCOG has had in the
  development of a broad band coalition. She encouraged the City Council to
  keep these and other issues in mind when considering the value of its
  membership in the SBCCOG.

C.  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN reported that he attended the Los Angeles
  Community Choice Energy (LACCE) meeting and explained the process for
  formation of the organization and the process by which individuals will be able
  to purchase renewable energy through LACCE. He noted that all energy users
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
AUGUST 8, 2017
   will be automatically enrolled in the program, but will have the ability opt out at
  any time with no penalty. After a brief discussion it was suggested that the
  LACCE engage the California Contract Cities Association and LA County
  Division of the League of California Cities to further spread the word about the
  organization.

D.  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF thanked staff for their work in planning and attending
  the National Night Out events that were held earlier this month. She also
  recognized and thanked the neighborhood hosts of the five events. COUNCIL
  MEMBER MITCHELL concurred with MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF.

13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS: This item provides the opportunity for Members
  of the City Council to request information on currently pending projects and/or
  issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration
  and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

A.  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF reminded everyone that the Hills Are Alive cross
  country runs are scheduled for Saturday, August 12 beginning at 8:00 a.m.
  Community Services Director Clark stated that the City is still taking
  registrations for the event.

B.  MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that the California Contract Cities Association
  annual Board of Directors meeting with the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s
  Department is scheduled for next week at the L.A. County Arboretum and
  welcomed all to attend.

15.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 8:30 p.m. MAYOR ZERUNYAN formally adjourned the City Council meeting
  to the next regular meeting of the City Council.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Douglas R. Prichard
City Clerk  City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
AUGUST 8, 2017
